app.title: micromorph - SEM morphology analysis
app.summary: A person picks the kind of structure in the sample, uploads one micrograph and chooses its magnification, which sets the pixel scale. The interface thresholds the image into foreground and background, sorts every background region by shape into spurious, real, ambiguous or noise, and lets the person tune the shape thresholds with sliders or presets while watching a colour-coded overlay. They then compare the initial and corrected masks, check the boundary contours against the raw image, and get size distributions with median and 95th percentile, which they download as summary and per-measurement CSVs and an HTML report.

task.text: Segment a micrograph into fiber and void, fix regions the threshold got wrong by their shape, and measure fiber diameter and pore size distributions for one image.

data.text: A single grayscale electron micrograph at a known magnification, turned into a binary mask and then into distributions of measured lengths
data.item: a connected dark region of the thresholded micrograph, classified by its shape descriptors

stage.text: segmenting and measuring micrographs after imaging, before comparing samples or batches

mechanism.text: Expandable steps run top to bottom, each drawing on the mask from the one before: shape sliders and presets recompute a colour-coded classification overlay and counts live, the corrected mask is set beside the initial one with a difference overlay and toggleable contours, and the final mask feeds distribution histograms, headline statistics and file downloads.

field.text: quantitative image analysis of fiber and pore morphology from SEM micrographs in materials science

workflow.name: segment an image, correct misclassified regions by shape, and measure size distributions

steps.step: choose the kind of structure being analysed
steps.here: a button grid from a morphology registry; active types switch the preset and the output vocabulary, planned types show a toast and a link to their tracking issue
upload a TIF/PNG/JPG micrograph and pick its magnification, which looks up µm per pixel; the bottom info bar is cropped off

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: background-subtracted Otsu threshold plus closing gives an initial fiber mask, shown next to the raw image with scale bars, threshold and area fraction

steps.step: classify regions and tune the rule until it looks right
steps.here: aspect ratio, solidity, circularity and noise-area sliders (or Default, Aggressive and Conservative presets) re-sort dark regions into pseudo-pore, real pore, ambiguous and noise on a red/blue/yellow overlay, with counts and QC warnings
initial and revised masks side by side with fiber area fractions, a green overlay of the flipped regions, and yellow contours drawn over the raw image to confirm the segmentation

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: fiber diameters from the distance-transform skeleton, void chord lengths from four-direction scan lines and inscribed-circle sizes, reported as d50, p95 and n with histograms
download results.csv (one summary row), distributions.csv (every measurement) and report.html

distinctive: dark bands inside thick fibers are flipped back to fiber when their shape is long, smooth and thin, which corrects a known imaging artifact
in stacked 3D mode, pore metrics are relabelled as void and flagged as upper bounds, both in the interface and in the exported column names
the pixel scale comes from the chosen magnification through an instrument calibration table, not from the image
the active preset is detected from the slider values and shown as Default, Aggressive, Conservative or Custom
